findings.title: Off-by-one error in totalPages computation causes a phantom empty last page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members with limit 50), this yields 3 instead of the correct 2 pages. Combined with the `next` action's offset calculation (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), a user can click 'next' from the real last page and land on an extra page whose offset equals `user_count`, which returns zero members from the server (since valid offsets are `0..user_count-1`). The pager will show e.g. 'Page 3/3' with no members listed, and `showingLast` never becomes true until this phantom page is reached. The correct formula should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Breaking change to /groups/:id/members.json response shape and default page size
findings.body: The `members` action used to return a plain serialized array for non-automatic groups (unbounded) and only paginated automatic groups at a default limit of 200. It now always returns a hash `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and defaults to a limit of 50 for every group, automatic or not. Any existing API consumer (mobile apps, external integrations, scripts) that expects the previous array response or expects to receive the full membership list for non-automatic groups will break or silently receive only the first 50 members with no indication that pagination occurred. This is a backward-incompatible API change that is not called out or versioned.

findings.title: No upper bound on client-supplied limit and no validation of offset for /groups/:id/members.json
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in the query with no maximum cap or minimum validation. A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` to retrieve an entire (potentially huge, e.g. 'everyone') group's membership in a single request, defeating the purpose of pagination and risking excessive serialization/DB load. A negative `offset` is also not guarded against, which can produce unexpected SQL (Postgres rejects negative OFFSET values), leading to a 500 error for malformed input on this public, non-admin endpoint.

findings.title: Membership mutation is persisted before the subsequent save-based success/failure check
findings.body: In `add_members`, `group.add(user)` is called in a loop (which persists the association immediately via the has_many collection), and only afterward is `group.save` checked to decide whether to render success or `render_json_error`. The same pattern exists in `remove_member` with `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`. If `group.save` fails for any unrelated reason (e.g. a validation on the group model), the membership change has already been committed to the database, yet the client is told the operation failed via `render_json_error`, producing an inconsistent/misleading response relative to the actual state of the data.

findings.title: No spec coverage added for the rewritten /groups/:id/members pagination behavior
findings.body: The `members` action was substantially rewritten: response shape changed to `{members:, meta:}`, pagination now applies uniformly to automatic and non-automatic groups, and the default limit changed from effectively unlimited (non-automatic) / 200 (automatic) to 50 for all groups. No corresponding spec file (e.g. groups_controller_spec.rb) was added or updated in this PR to verify the new `meta` payload, default/overridden limit and offset behavior, or the total count, leaving this behavior-changing rewrite untested.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember actions silently swallow AJAX failures
findings.body: Unlike `save` and `destroy`, which attach failure handlers that show a `bootbox.alert` with the server error, the `removeMember` and `addMembers` actions call `this.get('model').removeMember(member)` / `addMembers(usernames)` without attaching any rejection handler. If the request fails (e.g. a 422 for an automatic group, or a network error), the promise rejection is unhandled and the admin receives no feedback that the action did not take effect. Additionally the `addMembers` action leaves a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment, meaning the username input is never cleared after a successful add, which can lead to accidental duplicate submissions.
